text: Capability != authority.
Retrieval != evidence authority.
Every decision-relevant fact must have identifiable provenance.
Current state must not be inferred solely from historical success.
Historically valid evidence remains historically valid even when it no longer determines current state.
Superseded evidence must not control present state unless the mission explicitly requires historical reasoning.
Model confidence must not increase enterprise authority.
User assertion must not silently override authoritative enterprise state.
Unknown remains unknown unless an authorized evidence source resolves it.
Material evidence conflict must not be silently merged.
Equal-authority unresolved contradictions block, re-observe, or escalate according to policy.
A technically available tool does not establish execution permission.
Requester authority and execution authority are evaluated separately.
Recommendation must not be represented as approval.
Approval must not be represented as execution.
Successful tool invocation is not validated enterprise success without required readback.
Consequential actions must be attributable to an authority chain.
Every denied consequential action must have a machine-readable reason.
Every executed consequential action must produce a machine-correlatable execution receipt.
Validation defines durable success.
Policies dominate model preference.
Safety-critical mandatory evidence must not be removed for efficiency.
Benchmark ground truth must not be generated by the evaluated model.
Treatment results must not modify frozen benchmark expectations.
